title: CHECKPOINT — Break a Tool, Make the Agent Recover

content.goal: Add a tool that can fail, and make it fail on purpose.
content.why: The most-skipped competency is error handling. We will deliberately break a tool, then make ATLAS recover — errors as observations. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 7, section 7.3.)
content.verify: The file saves. The tool returns a clear, informative error for unknown topics instead of crashing — exactly what the theory calls "informative failures."

content.goal: Confirm the loop already feeds tool errors back as observations.
content.why: Because run_tool_call returns the error dict (rather than raising), your loop already hands it to the model as a tool result — the model SEES the failure and can adapt. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 7, section 7.3.)
content.verify: The file saves. Any tool failure — bad arguments, an exception, an unknown topic — now returns as an {"error": ...} observation the model can react to.

content.goal: Run a task that triggers the failure and watch ATLAS recover.
content.why: A resilient agent adapts to failure — retries with a different argument, or asks the user — instead of dying. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 7, section 7.3.)
content.code:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(run_agent("Tell me a fact about kangaroos. If that fails, tell me a fact about python instead."))
content.verify: ATLAS calls fetch_fact('kangaroos'), receives the error observation, and RECOVERS — either asking you to pick a known topic or falling back to 'python' as instructed. It does not crash. That recovery is the whole point of this checkpoint.
content.troubleshoot: If ATLAS gives up too early, add to the system prompt: "If a tool returns an error, adapt — try a different valid input or ask the user — do not abandon the goal." If it loops on the failing call, your repeated-call guard (Unit 5) stops it.

content.goal: Simulate a rate limit and add a simple retry-with-backoff around the model call.
content.why: Free tiers throttle you; robust code retries transient failures politely. This previews the reliability engineering of Ch 17. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 3 and Ch 17.)
content.verify: When the provider returns a transient error (like a 429 rate limit), ATLAS waits and retries with growing backoff instead of failing immediately. On a healthy connection it succeeds on the first attempt.
content.troubleshoot: Only retry TRANSIENT errors (timeouts, 429, 5xx). Do not retry a 401 (bad key) or 400 (bad request) — those will never succeed and waste your quota.

content.goal: PHASE 10 CHECKPOINT — a resilient first agent, complete.
content.why: You have exercised all four core competencies at a basic level: orchestration (the loop), tool integration, and — the hardest — error handling and recovery.
content.verify: All true — ATLAS runs a multi-step ReAct loop; it has a step limit and a repeated-call guard; tool failures return as observations and the agent recovers; transient provider errors are retried with backoff. Save your atlas.py. In Phase 11 you will give ATLAS memory, real document knowledge (RAG), a framework, MCP, and a specialist sub-agent.
